original_text: 道可道，非常道。
translated_text: The Way that can be spoken of is not the eternal Way.

original_text: 名可名，非常名。
translated_text: The name that can be named is not the eternal name.

original_text: 無名天地之始；有名萬物之母。
translated_text: The nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth. The named is the mother of the ten thousand things.

original_text: 故常無，欲以觀其妙；常有，欲以觀其徼。
translated_text: Therefore, always free from desire you can observe the mystery. Always filled with desire you can observe the manifestations.

original_text: 此兩者，同出而異名，同謂之玄。玄之又玄，眾妙之門。
translated_text: These two spring from the same source but differ in name; they appear dark and mysterious. Mystery of mysteries, the gate of all wonders.

original_text: 天下皆知美之為美，斯惡已。
translated_text: All the world knows beauty as beauty, yet this is only ugliness.

original_text: 皆知善之為善，斯不善已。
translated_text: All the world knows good as good, yet this is only evil.

original_text: 故有無相生，難易相成，長短相形，高下相傾，音聲相和，前後相隨。
translated_text: Therefore being and non-being produce each other. Difficult and easy complete each other. Long and short contrast each other. High and low depend on each other. Sound and tone harmonize with each other. Front and back follow each other.

original_text: 是以聖人處無為之事，行不言之教；
translated_text: Therefore the sage manages affairs without action and spreads teachings without words.

original_text: 萬物作焉而不辭，生而不有，為而不恃，功成而弗居。
translated_text: The ten thousand things rise and fall without cease, but he does not begin them. He acts but does not possess. He accomplishes but does not claim credit.

original_text: 夫唯弗居，是以不去。
translated_text: It is precisely because he does not claim credit that his credit never leaves him.

original_text: 不尚賢，使民不爭；
translated_text: Do not exalt the worthy, so that the people will not compete.

original_text: 不貴難得之貨，使民不為盜；
translated_text: Do not value rare goods, so that the people will not become thieves.

original_text: 不見可欲，使民心不亂。
translated_text: Do not display what is desirable, so that the people's hearts will not be disturbed.

original_text: 是以聖人之治，虛其心，實其腹，弱其志，強其骨。
translated_text: Therefore the sage governs by emptying their minds, filling their bellies, weakening their ambitions, and strengthening their bones.

original_text: 常使民無知無欲。
translated_text: He always keeps the people without knowledge and without desire.

original_text: 道沖，而用之或不盈。
translated_text: The Tao is like an empty vessel, yet it may be used without ever needing to be filled.

original_text: 淵兮，似萬物之宗；
translated_text: Deep, it seems to be the ancestor of the ten thousand things.

original_text: 挫其銳，解其紛，和其光，同其塵。
translated_text: Blunt the sharpness, untie the tangles, soften the light, become one with the dust.

original_text: 湛兮，似或存。
translated_text: Profound, it seems to exist forever.

original_text: 吾不知誰之子，象帝之先。
translated_text: I do not know whose child it is. It seems to be the ancestor of the gods.

original_text: 天地不仁，以萬物為芻狗；
translated_text: Heaven and earth are not humane; they treat the ten thousand things as straw dogs.

original_text: 聖人不仁，以百姓為芻狗。
translated_text: The sage is not humane; he treats the people as straw dogs.

original_text: 天地之間，其猶橐籥乎？
translated_text: Between heaven and earth, is it not like a bellows?

original_text: 虛而不屈，動而愈出。
translated_text: Empty yet inexhaustible, the more it moves, the more it produces.

original_text: 谷神不死，是謂玄牝。
translated_text: The spirit of the valley never dies. It is called the mysterious female.

original_text: 玄牝之門，是謂天地根。
translated_text: The gateway of the mysterious female is called the root of heaven and earth.

original_text: 天長地久。
translated_text: Heaven is eternal, earth endures.

original_text: 天地所以能長且久者，以其不自生，故能長生。
translated_text: The reason heaven and earth endure is that they do not live for themselves. Therefore they can live long.

original_text: 是以聖人後其身而身先；外其身而身存。
translated_text: Therefore the sage puts himself last and yet finds himself first. He stays outside and yet his self is preserved.

original_text: 非以其無私邪？故能成其私。
translated_text: Is it not because he is unselfish? That is why he can fulfill himself.

original_text: 上善若水。
translated_text: The highest good is like water.

original_text: 水善利萬物而不爭，處眾人之所惡，故幾於道。
translated_text: Water benefits all things and does not compete. It dwells in places that all disdain. Therefore it is close to the Tao.

original_text: 居善地，心善淵，與善仁，言善信，政善治，事善能，動善時。
translated_text: In dwelling, be close to the ground. In the heart, be deep. In relationships, be kind. In speech, be sincere. In governing, be just. In action, be capable. In timing, be appropriate.

original_text: 夫唯不爭，故無尤。
translated_text: It is precisely because he does not compete that he is without blame.

original_text: 持而盈之，不如其已；
translated_text: To hold and fill a cup to overflowing is not as good as stopping in time.

original_text: 揣而銳之，不可長保。
translated_text: To temper a blade to sharpness cannot be maintained for long.

original_text: 金玉滿堂，莫之能守；
translated_text: When gold and jade fill the hall, no one can guard them.

original_text: 富貴而驕，自遺其咎。
translated_text: Wealth and arrogance bring their own downfall.

original_text: 功遂身退，天之道也。
translated_text: When the work is done, withdraw. This is the Tao of heaven.

original_text: 載營魄抱一，能無離乎？
translated_text: In embracing the spirit and soul as one, can you keep them from separating?

original_text: 專氣致柔，能如嬰兒乎？
translated_text: In concentrating your breath to achieve suppleness, can you become like an infant?

original_text: 滌除玄覽，能無疵乎？
translated_text: In cleansing your inner vision, can you become without blemish?

original_text: 愛民治國，能無為乎？
translated_text: In loving the people and governing the state, can you do so without action?

original_text: 天門開闔，能為雌乎？
translated_text: In opening and closing the gates of heaven, can you be like a female?

original_text: 明白四達，能無知乎？
translated_text: In understanding all things with clarity, can you remain without knowledge?

original_text: 三十輻共一轂，當其無，有車之用。
translated_text: Thirty spokes share one hub. It is the space where there is nothing that gives the wheel its use.

original_text: 埏埴以為器，當其無，有器之用。
translated_text: Clay is shaped into a vessel. It is the space where there is nothing that gives the vessel its use.

original_text: 鑿戶牖以為室，當其無，有室之用。
translated_text: Doors and windows are cut out to make a room. It is the space where there is nothing that gives the room its use.

original_text: 故有之以為利，無之以為用。
translated_text: Therefore benefit comes from what is there; use comes from what is not there.

original_text: 五色令人目盲；
translated_text: The five colors blind the eye.

original_text: 五音令人耳聾；
translated_text: The five tones deafen the ear.

original_text: 五味令人口爽；
translated_text: The five flavors dull the palate.

original_text: 馳騁畋獵，令人心發狂；
translated_text: Racing and hunting madden the mind.

original_text: 難得之貨，令人行妨。
translated_text: Rare goods obstruct one's way.

original_text: 是以聖人為腹不為目，故去彼取此。
translated_text: Therefore the sage is for the belly and not for the eye. He lets go of that and chooses this.

original_text: 寵辱若驚，貴大患若身。
translated_text: Favor and disgrace are both alarming. Great misfortune is like the self.

original_text: 何謂寵辱若驚？寵為下，得之若驚，失之若驚，是謂寵辱若驚。
translated_text: What is meant by 'favor and disgrace are both alarming'? Favor is low. Gaining it is alarming. Losing it is alarming. This is what is meant by 'favor and disgrace are both alarming.'

original_text: 何謂貴大患若身？吾所以有大患者，為吾有身，及吾無身，吾有何患？
translated_text: What is meant by 'great misfortune is like the self'? The reason I have great misfortune is that I have a self. If I had no self, what misfortune could I have?

original_text: 故貴以身為天下，若可寄天下；愛以身為天下，若可託天下。
translated_text: Therefore those who value themselves for the sake of the world can be entrusted with the world. Those who love themselves for the sake of the world can be given the world.

original_text: 視之不見，名曰夷；聽之不聞，名曰希；搏之不得，名曰微。
translated_text: Look at it and it cannot be seen — that is called the invisible. Listen to it and it cannot be heard — that is called the inaudible. Grasp at it and it cannot be held — that is called the intangible.

original_text: 此三者不可致詰，故混而為一。
translated_text: These three cannot be further examined, and so they are blended into one.

original_text: 其上不皦，其下不昧。
translated_text: Its top is not bright; its bottom is not dark.

original_text: 繩繩兮不可名，復歸於無物。
translated_text: Stretching endlessly, it cannot be named. It returns to nothingness.

original_text: 是謂無狀之狀，無物之象，是謂惚恍。
translated_text: This is called the form without form, the image without substance. It is called the vague and elusive.

original_text: 迎之不見其首，隨之不見其後。
translated_text: Meet it and you cannot see its front. Follow it and you cannot see its back.

original_text: 執古之道，以御今之有。能知古始，是謂道紀。
translated_text: Hold fast to the Tao of old to govern the present. To know the ancient beginning is called the thread of the Tao.

original_text: 古之善為士者，微妙玄通，深不可識。
translated_text: In ancient times those who practiced the Tao skillfully were subtly mysterious, profoundly wise, and too deep to be understood.

original_text: 夫唯不可識，故強為之容：
translated_text: Since they cannot be understood, I can only describe them:

original_text: 豫兮若冬涉川；猶兮若畏四鄰；儼兮其若客；渙兮其若凌釋；敦兮其若樸；曠兮其若谷；混兮其若濁；
translated_text: Cautious, like wading across a stream in winter. Hesitant, like fearing the neighbors on all sides. Dignified, like a guest. Loose, like melting ice. Simple, like uncarved wood. Open, like a valley. Confused, like muddy water.

original_text: 孰能濁以靜之徐清？孰能安以動之徐生？
translated_text: Who can be still and wait for the mud to settle? Who can be at rest and wait for life to arise?

original_text: 保此道者，不欲盈。夫唯不盈，故能蔽而新成。
translated_text: Those who keep to the Tao do not seek to be full. Since they are not full, they can be worn out and yet ever new.

original_text: 致虛極，守靜篤。
translated_text: Attain utmost emptiness. Maintain perfect stillness.

original_text: 萬物並作，吾以觀復。
translated_text: The ten thousand things rise together, and I watch their return.

original_text: 夫物芸芸，各復歸其根。
translated_text: Flourishing as they are, each returns to its root.

original_text: 歸根曰靜，靜曰復命。
translated_text: Returning to the root is called stillness. Stillness is called returning to destiny.

original_text: 復命曰常，知常曰明。
translated_text: Returning to destiny is called the constant. To know the constant is called illumination.

original_text: 太上，不知有之；
translated_text: The best leaders are those the people barely know exist.

original_text: 其次，親而譽之；
translated_text: The next best are loved and praised.

original_text: 其次，畏之；
translated_text: The next are feared.

original_text: 其次，侮之。信不足焉，有不信焉。
translated_text: The next are despised. When there is not enough trust, there is no trust.

original_text: 大道廢，有仁義；
translated_text: When the great Tao is abandoned, there is benevolence and righteousness.

original_text: 智慧出，有大偽；
translated_text: When cleverness and knowledge appear, there is great hypocrisy.

original_text: 六親不和，有孝慈；
translated_text: When the six relationships are not in harmony, there is filial piety and love.

original_text: 國家昏亂，有忠臣。
translated_text: When the state is in disorder, there are loyal ministers.

original_text: 絕聖棄智，民利百倍；
translated_text: Abandon sagacity and discard cleverness, and the people will benefit a hundredfold.

original_text: 絕仁棄義，民復孝慈；
translated_text: Abandon benevolence and discard righteousness, and the people will return to filial piety and love.

original_text: 絕巧棄利，盜賊無有。
translated_text: Abandon cunning and discard profit, and there will be no thieves or robbers.

original_text: 絕學無憂。
translated_text: Abandon learning and there will be no sorrow.

original_text: 唯之與阿，相去幾何？
translated_text: How much difference is there between yes and no?

original_text: 美之與惡，相去若何？
translated_text: How far apart are good and evil?

original_text: 人之所畏，不可不畏。
translated_text: What people fear, one must also fear.

original_text: 荒兮，其未央哉！
translated_text: It is so vast! It seems to have no end!

original_text: 孔德之容，惟道是從。
translated_text: The great virtue follows only the Tao.

original_text: 道之為物，惟恍惟惚。
translated_text: The Tao as a thing is vague and elusive.

original_text: 惚兮恍兮，其中有象；恍兮惚兮，其中有物。
translated_text: Elusive and vague, yet within it there is form. Vague and elusive, yet within it there is substance.

original_text: 窈兮冥兮，其中有精；其精甚真，其中有信。
translated_text: Dark and profound, yet within it there is essence. That essence is very real, and within it there is trust.

original_text: 曲則全，枉則直，窪則盈，敝則新，少則得，多則惑。
translated_text: To yield is to be preserved whole. To be bent is to become straight. To be emptied is to be filled. To be worn is to be renewed. To have little is to gain. To have much is to be confused.

original_text: 是以聖人抱一為天下式。
translated_text: Therefore the sage embraces the one and becomes the pattern of the world.

original_text: 不自見，故明；不自是，故彰；不自伐，故有功；不自矜，故長。
translated_text: He does not show himself, and so is clear. He does not assert himself, and so is distinguished. He does not boast, and so has merit. He does not brag, and so endures.

original_text: 夫唯不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。
translated_text: It is precisely because he does not compete that no one under heaven can compete with him.

original_text: 古之所謂曲則全者，豈虛言哉！誠全而歸之。
translated_text: Is the ancient saying 'to yield is to be preserved whole' empty words? Truly, it will be wholly attained.

original_text: 希言自然。
translated_text: Few words are natural.

original_text: 故飄風不終朝，驟雨不終日。
translated_text: Therefore a whirlwind does not last all morning. A sudden rain does not last all day.

original_text: 孰為此者？天地。天地尚不能久，而況於人乎？
translated_text: Who creates such things? Heaven and earth. If even heaven and earth cannot make things last forever, how much less can man?

original_text: 企者不立；跨者不行；
translated_text: He who stands on tiptoe does not stand firm. He who rushes ahead does not walk far.

original_text: 自見者不明；自是者不彰；自伐者無功；自矜者不長。
translated_text: He who displays himself does not shine. He who asserts himself is not distinguished. He who boasts gains no merit. He who brags does not endure.

original_text: 其在道也，曰餘食贅行。
translated_text: From the point of view of the Tao, these are like leftover food and useless growth.

original_text: 物或惡之，故有道者不處。
translated_text: The things all detest, and one who has the Tao does not stay with them.

original_text: 有物混成，先天地生。寂兮寥兮，獨立而不改，周行而不殆，可以為天地母。吾不知其名，強字之曰道，強為之名曰大。
translated_text: There was something undifferentiated and yet complete, which existed before heaven and earth. Soundless and formless, it depends on nothing and does not change. It operates everywhere and is never exhausted. It may be considered the mother of the universe. I do not know its name. I call it Tao. I am forced to give it a name — I call it Great.

original_text: 大曰逝，逝曰遠，遠曰反。
translated_text: Great means flowing away. Flowing away means far. Far means returning.

original_text: 故道大，天大，地大，人亦大。域中有四大，而人居其一焉。
translated_text: Therefore Tao is great. Heaven is great. Earth is great. Man is also great. Within the universe there are four greats, and man is one of them.

original_text: 人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然。
translated_text: Man follows earth. Earth follows heaven. Heaven follows the Tao. The Tao follows its own nature.

original_text: 重為輕根，靜為躁君。
translated_text: Weight is the root of lightness. Stillness is the master of restlessness.

original_text: 是以聖人終日行不離輜重。雖有榮觀，燕處超然。
translated_text: Therefore the sage travels all day without leaving his baggage. Though there are luxurious sights, he remains composed and transcendent.

original_text: 奈何萬乘之主，而以身輕天下？輕則失根，躁則失君。
translated_text: How can the lord of a great state make light of his own body? Lightness loses the root. Restlessness loses the master.

original_text: 善行無轍跡；善言無瑕謫；
translated_text: A good traveler leaves no tracks. A good speaker makes no slips.

original_text: 善數不用籌策；善閉無關楗而不可開；善結無繩約而不可解。
translated_text: A good counter needs no tallies. A good door needs no lock yet cannot be opened. A good knot needs no rope yet cannot be untied.

original_text: 是以聖人常善救人，故無棄人；常善救物，故無棄物。是謂襲明。
translated_text: Therefore the sage is always good at saving people, and therefore nobody is abandoned. He is always good at saving things, and therefore nothing is wasted. This is called hidden clarity.

original_text: 善人者，不善人之師；不善人者，善人之資。
translated_text: The good person is the teacher of the bad person, and the bad person is the material of the good person.

original_text: 不貴其師，不愛其資，雖智大迷，是謂要妙。
translated_text: He who does not respect his teacher, he who does not care for his material, though he may be clever, is greatly confused. This is called the essential mystery.

original_text: 知其雄，守其雌，為天下谿。
translated_text: Know the strong, but keep to the lowly. Be the stream of the world.

original_text: 為天下谿，常德不離，復歸於嬰兒。
translated_text: Being the stream of the world, you will not lose the eternal virtue, and will return to the state of infancy.

original_text: 知其白，守其黑，為天下式。
translated_text: Know the bright, but keep to the dark. Be the pattern of the world.

original_text: 為天下式，常德不忒，復歸於無極。
translated_text: Being the pattern of the world, you will not err, and will return to the infinite.

original_text: 知其榮，守其辱，為天下谷。
translated_text: Know the honored, but keep to the lowly. Be the valley of the world.

original_text: 將欲取天下而為之，吾見其不得已。
translated_text: If you want to take hold of the world and act on it, I see that you will not succeed.

original_text: 天下神器，不可為也，不可執也。為者敗之，執者失之。
translated_text: The world is a sacred vessel. It cannot be acted upon. He who acts on it will fail. He who grasps it will lose it.

original_text: 故物或行或隨；或歔或吹；或強或羸；或載或隳。
translated_text: Therefore things sometimes go forward and sometimes follow. Sometimes blow hot and sometimes blow cold. Sometimes strong and sometimes weak. Sometimes flourish and sometimes collapse.

original_text: 以道佐人主者，不以兵強天下。其事好還。
translated_text: He who assists the ruler with the Tao does not use force to overpower the world. Such things tend to recoil.

original_text: 師之所處，荊棘生焉。大軍之後，必有凶年。
translated_text: Where armies camp, brambles grow. After a great army, there is always a year of famine.

original_text: 善有果而已，不以取強。
translated_text: A good one achieves results and that is all. He does not use force to overpower.

original_text: 果而勿矜，果而勿伐，果而勿驕，果而不得已，果而勿強。
translated_text: Achieve results but do not be arrogant. Achieve results but do not boast. Achieve results but do not be proud. Achieve results only because there is no alternative. Achieve results but do not use force.

original_text: 夫兵者，不祥之器，物或惡之，故有道者不處。
translated_text: Weapons are instruments of ill omen. The things all detest them, and one who has the Tao does not stay with them.

original_text: 君子居則貴左，用兵則貴右。兵者不祥之器，非君子之器，不得已而用之，恬淡為上。
translated_text: The gentleman values the left in peacetime, but the right in war. Weapons are instruments of ill omen, not the instruments of the gentleman. He uses them only when there is no alternative, and values tranquility above all.

original_text: 勝而不美，而美之者，是樂殺人。
translated_text: To be victorious is not beautiful. He who finds beauty in victory delights in killing.

original_text: 夫樂殺人者，則不可得志於天下矣。
translated_text: He who delights in killing cannot achieve his will in the world.

original_text: 道常無名，樸雖小，天下莫能臣。
translated_text: The Tao is always nameless. Though the uncarved block is small, no one under heaven can make it submit.

original_text: 侯王若能守之，萬物將自賓。
translated_text: If lords and kings can keep to it, the ten thousand things will naturally submit.

original_text: 天地相合，以降甘露，民莫之令而自均。
translated_text: When heaven and earth unite, sweet dew descends. Without anyone's command, it falls evenly on all.

original_text: 始制有名，名亦既有，夫亦將知止。知止可以不殆。
translated_text: When ordering begins, names arise. Once names exist, one must know where to stop. Knowing where to stop, one can be free from danger.

original_text: 知人者智，自知者明。
translated_text: To know others is wisdom. To know yourself is enlightenment.

original_text: 勝人者有力，自勝者強。
translated_text: To overcome others is strength. To overcome yourself is true power.

original_text: 知足者富。
translated_text: He who knows contentment is rich.

original_text: 強行者有志。不失其所者久。死而不亡者壽。
translated_text: He who perseveres has will. He who does not lose his place endures. He who dies but does not perish has longevity.

original_text: 大道汎兮，其可左右。
translated_text: The great Tao flows everywhere. It can go either left or right.

original_text: 萬物恃之以生而不辭，功成而不有。
translated_text: The ten thousand things depend on it for life, yet it does not abandon them. It accomplishes its work, yet does not claim credit.

original_text: 衣養萬物而不為主，常無欲，可名於小；萬物歸焉而不為主，可名為大。
translated_text: It nourishes all things yet does not act as master. Always free from desire, it may be called small. The ten thousand things return to it yet it does not act as master. It may be called great.

original_text: 以其終不自為大，故能成其大。
translated_text: It is precisely because it never seeks greatness that it can accomplish its greatness.

original_text: 執大象，天下往。往而不害，安平泰。
translated_text: Hold fast to the great image, and the world will come to you. Coming without harm, it brings peace and safety.

original_text: 樂與餌，過客止。道之出口，淡乎其無味。
translated_text: Music and fine food make the passing traveler stop. The words of the Tao are bland and tasteless.

original_text: 視之不足見，聽之不足聞，用之不足既。
translated_text: Look at it and it cannot be seen. Listen to it and it cannot be heard. Use it and it cannot be exhausted.

original_text: 將欲歙之，必故張之；將欲弱之，必故強之；
translated_text: If you want to shrink something, you must first expand it. If you want to weaken something, you must first strengthen it.

original_text: 將欲廢之，必故興之；將欲取之，必故與之。是謂微明。
translated_text: If you want to overthrow something, you must first raise it up. If you want to take something, you must first give to it. This is called subtle clarity.

original_text: 柔弱勝剛強。
translated_text: The soft and weak overcome the hard and strong.

original_text: 魚不可脫於淵，國之利器不可以示人。
translated_text: Fish cannot be separated from the deep. The instruments of state power cannot be shown to others.

original_text: 道常無為而無不為。
translated_text: The Tao never acts, yet nothing is left undone.

original_text: 侯王若能守之，萬物將自化。
translated_text: If lords and kings can keep to it, the ten thousand things will transform naturally.

original_text: 化而欲作，吾將鎮之以無名之樸。無名之樸，夫亦將無欲。不欲以靜，天下將自正。
translated_text: If transformation gives rise to desire, I will pacify it with the nameless uncarved block. The nameless uncarved block will also bring freedom from desire. Free from desire and attained to stillness, the world will naturally be at peace.

original_text: 上德不德，是以有德；下德不失德，是以無德。
translated_text: Superior virtue is not virtuous, and therefore has virtue. Inferior virtue never loses virtue, and therefore has no virtue.

original_text: 上德無為而無以為；下德無為而有以為。
translated_text: Superior virtue acts without acting and has no purpose. Inferior virtue acts with purpose.

original_text: 上仁為之而無以為；上義為之而有以為。
translated_text: Superior benevolence acts without purpose. Superior righteousness acts with purpose.

original_text: 上禮為之而莫之應，則攘臂而扔之。
translated_text: Superior ritual acts, and when no one responds, rolls up his sleeves and forces compliance.

original_text: 故失道而後德，失德而後仁，失仁而後義，失義而後禮。夫禮者，忠信之薄，而亂之首。
translated_text: Therefore lose the Tao and then virtue is sought. Lose virtue and then benevolence is sought. Lose benevolence and then righteousness is sought. Lose righteousness and then ritual is sought. Ritual is the thinning of loyalty and trust, and the beginning of disorder.

original_text: 昔之得一者：天得一以清；地得一以寧；神得一以靈；谷得一以盈；萬物得一以生；侯王得一以為天下貞。
translated_text: Those in the past who attained the one: heaven attained it and became clear. Earth attained it and became stable. The spirits attained it and became divine. The valleys attained it and became full. The ten thousand things attained it and came to life. Lords and kings attained it and brought balance to the world.

original_text: 其致之也，謂天無以清，將恐裂；地無以寧，將恐廢；神無以靈，將恐歇；谷無以盈，將恐竭；萬物無以生，將恐滅；侯王無以正，將恐蹶。
translated_text: To extend this further: if heaven were not clear, it would fear cracking; if earth were not stable, it would fear collapsing; if the spirits were not divine, they would fear ceasing; if the valleys were not full, they would fear drying up; if the ten thousand things did not live, they would fear extinction; if lords and kings did not hold the highest place, they would fear stumbling.

original_text: 故貴以賤為本，高以下為基。
translated_text: Therefore nobility is rooted in lowliness. The high is founded on the low.

original_text: 是以侯王自稱孤、寡、不穀。此非以賤為本邪？非乎？
translated_text: Therefore lords and kings call themselves orphaned, lonely, and unworthy. Is this not using lowliness as the root? Is it not?

original_text: 故至譽無譽。是故不欲琭琭如玉，珞珞如石。
translated_text: Therefore the highest praise is no praise. Therefore do not wish to be sparkling like jade, but be dull like rock.

original_text: 反者道之動；弱者道之用。
translated_text: Return is the movement of the Tao. Weakness is the function of the Tao.

original_text: 天下萬物生於有，有生於無。
translated_text: The ten thousand things under heaven are born of being. Being is born of non-being.

original_text: 上士聞道，勤而行之；中士聞道，若存若亡；下士聞道，大笑之。不笑不足以為道。
translated_text: When the highest hear of the Tao, they practice it diligently. When the middle hear of the Tao, they half-believe and half-doubt. When the lowest hear of the Tao, they laugh out loud. If they did not laugh at it, it would not be worthy of the Tao.

original_text: 故建言有之：明道若昧；進道若退；夷道若顢；上德若谷；廣德若不足；建德若偷；質真若渝；大白若辱；大方無隅；大器晚成；大音希聲；大象無形。
translated_text: Therefore the ancient words say: The bright Tao seems dark. The advancing Tao seems to retreat. The level Tao seems uneven. The highest virtue seems like a valley. The broadest virtue seems deficient. The strongest virtue seems lazy. The purest truth seems changeable. The greatest whiteness seems soiled. The greatest square has no corners. The greatest vessel takes long to complete. The greatest sound is silent. The greatest image has no form.

original_text: 道隱無名。
translated_text: The Tao is hidden and nameless.

original_text: 夫唯道，善貸且成。
translated_text: It is only the Tao that is good at lending and completing.

original_text: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。
translated_text: The Tao gives birth to One. One gives birth to Two. Two gives birth to Three. Three gives birth to the ten thousand things.

original_text: 萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和。
translated_text: The ten thousand things carry yin and embrace yang, and through the blending of qi they achieve harmony.

original_text: 人之所惡，唯孤、寡、不穀，而王公以為稱。
translated_text: What people despise — orphaned, lonely, and unworthy — are the very terms lords and kings use for themselves.

original_text: 故物或損之而益，或益之而損。
translated_text: Therefore some things are diminished by being increased, and increased by being diminished.

original_text: 天下之至柔，馳騁天下之至堅。
translated_text: The most supple thing under heaven overcomes the hardest thing under heaven.

original_text: 無有入無間，吾是以知無為之有益。
translated_text: Non-being enters where there are no gaps. Therefore I know the benefit of non-action.

original_text: 不言之教，無為之益，天下希及之。
translated_text: The teaching of non-speech, the benefit of non-action — few under heaven can attain to this.

original_text: 名與身孰親？身與貨孰多？得與亡孰病？
translated_text: Which is closer, name or self? Which is more valuable, self or possessions? Which is more harmful, gain or loss?

original_text: 甚愛必大費；多藏必厚亡。
translated_text: Great love entails great expense. Much hoarding brings heavy loss.

original_text: 故知足不辱，知止不殆，可以長久。
translated_text: Therefore know contentment and you will not suffer. Know when to stop and you will be free from danger. Thus you may endure.

original_text: 大成若缺，其用不弊。大盈若沖，其用不窮。
translated_text: Great perfection seems flawed, yet its use is never exhausted. Great fullness seems empty, yet its use is never depleted.

original_text: 大直若屈，大巧若拙，大辯若訥。
translated_text: Great straightness seems bent. Great skill seems clumsy. Great eloquence seems stammering.

original_text: 靜勝躁，寒勝熱。清靜為天下正。
translated_text: Stillness overcomes restlessness. Cold overcomes heat. Clarity and stillness bring the world to balance.

original_text: 天下有道，卻走馬以糞。天下無道，戎馬生於郊。
translated_text: When the world has the Tao, galloping horses are used to fertilize the fields. When the world lacks the Tao, war horses are bred on the borders.

original_text: 天下有道，卻走馬以糞。天下無道，戎馬生於郊。
translated_text: When the world has the Tao, galloping horses are used to fertilize the fields. When the world lacks the Tao, war horses are bred on the borders.

original_text: 罪莫大於可欲；禍莫大於不知足；咎莫大於欲得。
translated_text: No crime is greater than yielding to desire. No disaster is greater than not knowing contentment. No fault is greater than wanting to possess.

original_text: 故知足之足，常足矣。
translated_text: Therefore the contentment of knowing contentment is always contentment.

original_text: 不出戶，知天下；不窺牖，見天道。
translated_text: Without going outside, you can know the world. Without looking through the window, you can see the heavenly Tao.

original_text: 其出彌遠，其知彌少。
translated_text: The further you go, the less you know.

original_text: 是以聖人不行而知，不見而明，不為而成。
translated_text: Therefore the sage knows without traveling, sees without looking, and accomplishes without acting.

original_text: 為學日益，為道日損。損之又損，以至於無為。
translated_text: In pursuit of learning, every day something is acquired. In pursuit of Tao, every day something is dropped. Drop and drop again, until one reaches non-action.

original_text: 無為而無不為。
translated_text: Through non-action, nothing is left undone.

original_text: 取天下常以無事，及其有事，不足以取天下。
translated_text: To govern the world, one must always act without interference. If one interferes, one is not fit to govern the world.

original_text: 聖人無常心，以百姓心為心。
translated_text: The sage has no fixed mind. He takes the mind of the people as his mind.

original_text: 善者，吾善之；不善者，吾亦善之；德善。
translated_text: To the good, I am good. To the not good, I am also good. This is the goodness of virtue.

original_text: 信者，吾信之；不信者，吾亦信之；德信。
translated_text: To the trustworthy, I am trustworthy. To the untrustworthy, I am also trustworthy. This is the trustworthiness of virtue.

original_text: 聖人在天下，歙歙焉，為天下渾其心。百姓皆注其耳目，聖人皆孩之。
translated_text: The sage lives in the world, cautiously shrinking, and harmonizes his mind for the world. The people all focus their ears and eyes on him, and the sage treats them all as children.

original_text: 出生入死。
translated_text: Life leads into death.

original_text: 生之徒，十有三；死之徒，十有三；人之生，動之於死地，亦十有三。
translated_text: Of those who live, three out of ten follow the path of life. Three out of ten follow the path of death. And of those who live, three out of ten also move toward death.

original_text: 夫何故？以其生生之厚。
translated_text: Why is this? Because they try too hard to sustain life.

original_text: 道生之，德畜之，物形之，勢成之。
translated_text: The Tao gives them birth. Virtue nurtures them. Matter gives them form. Circumstances complete them.

original_text: 是以萬物莫不尊道而貴德。
translated_text: Therefore the ten thousand things all honor the Tao and value virtue.

original_text: 道之尊，德之貴，夫莫之命而常自然。
translated_text: The honor of the Tao and the value of virtue are not bestowed by anyone, but are always natural.

original_text: 故道生之，德畜之；長之育之；亭之毒之；養之覆之。
translated_text: Therefore the Tao gives them birth, virtue nurtures them, they grow and are nourished, they are sheltered and protected, they are fed and sheltered.

original_text: 天下有始，以為天下母。
translated_text: The world had a beginning, which may be called the mother of the world.

original_text: 既得其母，以知其子，既知其子，復守其母，沒身不殆。
translated_text: Having found the mother, you can know her children. Having known the children, return to protect the mother. Then you will be free from danger to the end of your life.

original_text: 塞其兌，閉其門，終身不勤。開其兌，濟其事，終身不救。
translated_text: Block the openings, shut the doors, and you will not toil all your life. Open the openings, busy yourself with affairs, and you cannot be saved.

original_text: 見小曰明，守柔曰強。用其光，復歸其明，無遺身殃；是為襲常。
translated_text: To see the small is called clarity. To keep to the weak is called strength. Use its light, return to its clarity. Do not leave a legacy of calamity for yourself. This is called following the constant.

original_text: 使我介然有知，行於大道，唯施是畏。
translated_text: If I had the slightest knowledge, I would walk the great Tao and fear only to stray from it.

original_text: 大道甚夷，而人好徑。
translated_text: The great Tao is very smooth, yet people prefer the shortcuts.

original_text: 朝甚除，田甚蕪，倉甚虛；服文采，帶利劍，厭飲食，財貨有餘；是謂盜誇。非道也哉！
translated_text: The court is well adorned, the fields are very overgrown, the granaries are very empty. Wearing fine clothes, carrying sharp swords, gorging on food and drink, hoarding wealth and goods beyond measure — this is called the pride of thieves. It is not the Tao!

original_text: 善建者不拔，善抱者不脫，子孫以祭祀不輟。
translated_text: What is firmly established cannot be uprooted. What is firmly held cannot slip away. Descendants will continue the sacrifice unceasingly.

original_text: 修之於身，其德乃真；修之於家，其德乃餘；修之於鄉，其德乃長；修之於邦，其德乃豐；修之於天下，其德乃普。
translated_text: Cultivated in the self, virtue is genuine. Cultivated in the family, virtue is abundant. Cultivated in the village, virtue is lasting. Cultivated in the state, virtue is abundant. Cultivated in the world, virtue is universal.

original_text: 故以身觀身，以家觀家，以鄉觀鄉，以邦觀邦，以天下觀天下。
translated_text: Therefore observe the self by observing the self. Observe the family by observing the family. Observe the village by observing the village. Observe the state by observing the state. Observe the world by observing the world.

original_text: 吾何以知天下然哉？以此。
translated_text: How do I know the world is like this? By this.

original_text: 含德之厚，比於赤子。
translated_text: One who possesses virtue in abundance is like an infant.

original_text: 毒蟲不螫，猛獸不據，攫鳥不搏。
translated_text: Poisonous insects do not sting. Fierce beasts do not attack. Birds of prey do not strike.

original_text: 骨弱筋柔而握固。未知牝牡之合而朘作，精之至也。終日號而不嗄，和之至也。
translated_text: His bones are weak, his sinews soft, yet his grasp is firm. Not knowing the union of male and female, his essence is at its peak. He can cry all day without becoming hoarse — his harmony is at its peak.

original_text: 知和曰常，知常曰明。益生曰祥。心使氣曰強。物壯則老，謂之不道，不道早已。
translated_text: To know harmony is called the constant. To know the constant is called illumination. To try to increase life is called a curse. To let the mind command the qi is called strength. When things reach their prime, they begin to age. This is called not following the Tao. Not following the Tao leads to early end.

original_text: 知者不言，言者不知。
translated_text: Those who know do not speak. Those who speak do not know.

original_text: 塞其兌，閉其門，挫其銳，解其紛，和其光，同其塵，是謂玄同。
translated_text: Block the openings, shut the doors, blunt the sharpness, untie the tangles, soften the light, become one with the dust. This is called the mysterious unity.

original_text: 故不可得而親，不可得而疏；不可得而利，不可得而害；不可得而貴，不可得而賤。故為天下貴。
translated_text: Therefore one cannot be亲近, nor estranged. One cannot be benefited, nor harmed. One cannot be honored, nor degraded. Therefore he is valued by all under heaven.

original_text: 以正治國，以奇用兵，以無事取天下。
translated_text: Govern the state with correctness. Use strategy in war. Win the world through non-interference.

original_text: 吾何以知其然哉？以此：天下多忌諱，而民彌貧；人多利器，國家滋昏；人多伎巧，奇物滋起；法令滋彰，盜賊多有。
translated_text: How do I know this is so? By this: the more prohibitions there are, the poorer the people become. The more weapons there are, the more the state falls into disorder. The more cleverness there is, the more strange things arise. The more laws are proclaimed, the more thieves and robbers appear.

original_text: 故聖人云：我無為，而民自化；我好靜，而民自正；我無事，而民自富；我無欲，而民自樸。
translated_text: Therefore the sage says: I do not interfere, and the people transform themselves. I love stillness, and the people rectify themselves. I do not meddle, and the people prosper on their own. I am without desire, and the people return to simplicity on their own.

original_text: 其政悶悶，其民淳淳；其政察察，其民缺缺。
translated_text: When government is dull and lazy, the people are simple and honest. When government is sharp and shrewd, the people are cunning and deficient.

original_text: 禍兮，福之所倚，福兮，禍之所伏。孰知其極？其無正也。
translated_text: Misfortune — fortune leans upon it. Fortune — misfortune hides beneath it. Who knows their ultimate end? There is no standard.

original_text: 正復為奇，善復為妖。人之迷，其日固久。
translated_text: The straight becomes crooked. The good becomes corrupt. People's confusion has lasted a long time.

original_text: 是以聖人方而不割，廉而不劌，直而不肆，光而不耀。
translated_text: Therefore the sage is upright but not cutting, sharp but not piercing, straight but not unrestrained, bright but not blinding.

original_text: 治人事天，莫若嗇。
translated_text: In governing people and serving heaven, nothing surpasses moderation.

original_text: 夫為嗇，是謂早服；早服謂之重積德；重積德則無不克；無不克則莫知其極；莫知其極，可以有國；有國之母，可以長久。
translated_text: Moderation means early preparation. Early preparation means accumulating virtue. Accumulating virtue means nothing is impossible. Nothing impossible means no limit. No limit means one can hold the state. Having the mother of the state means one can endure.

original_text: 是謂深根固柢，長生久視之道。
translated_text: This is called deepening the root and firming the foundation — the way of long life and lasting vision.

original_text: 治大國，若烹小鮮。
translated_text: Governing a great state is like cooking a small fish.

original_text: 以道蒞天下，其鬼不神；非其鬼不神，其神不傷人；非其神不傷人，聖人亦不傷人。
translated_text: When the Tao rules the world, ghosts have no power. It is not that the ghosts have no power, but that their power does not harm people. It is not that their power does not harm people, but the sage does not harm people either.

original_text: 夫兩不相傷，故德交歸焉。
translated_text: Since neither harms the other, virtue converges upon them both.

original_text: 大國者下流，天下之交，天下之牝。牝常以靜勝牡，以靜為下。
translated_text: A great state is like a low-lying place where all streams converge — the female of the world. The female always overcomes the male through stillness, by making herself lower through stillness.

original_text: 故大國以下小國，則取小國；小國以下大國，則取大國。
translated_text: Therefore a great state that is humble toward a small state wins the small state. A small state that is humble toward a great state wins the great state.

original_text: 故或下以取，或下而取。大國不過欲兼畜人，小國不過欲入事人。夫兩者各得所欲，大者宜為下。
translated_text: So one wins by being humble, and the other wins by being humble. A great state desires only to shelter people. A small state desires only to serve people. Both get what they desire, but the greater state should place itself lower.

original_text: 道者萬物之奧，善人之寶，不善人之所保。
translated_text: The Tao is the sanctuary of all things, the treasure of the good person, and the refuge of the bad person.

original_text: 美言可以市尊，美行可以加人。人之不善，何棄之有？
translated_text: Fine words can win respect. Fine actions can elevate others. Even if a person is not good, why should he be abandoned?

original_text: 故立天子，置三公，雖有拱璧以先駟馬，不如坐進此道。
translated_text: Therefore when installing a sovereign or establishing ministers, even with jade preceded by a team of horses, it is better to sit down and offer this Tao.

original_text: 古之所以貴此道者何？不曰：以求得，有罪以免邪？故為天下貴。
translated_text: Why did the ancients value this Tao? Did they not say: by seeking you can find it, and by having sin you can be forgiven? Therefore it is valued by all under heaven.

original_text: 為無為，事無事，味無味。
translated_text: Act through non-action. Handle affairs without interference. Find flavor in the tasteless.

original_text: 圖難於其易，為大於其細；天下難事，必作於易，天下大事，必作於細。是以聖人終不為大，故能成其大。
translated_text: Plan for the difficult while it is still easy. Do great things while they are still small. All difficult things under heaven start from the easy. All great things under heaven start from the small. Therefore the sage never acts greatly, and so accomplishes greatness.

original_text: 輕諾必寡信，多易必多難。是以聖人猶難之，故終無難矣。
translated_text: Easy promises必 lose trust. Treating many things as easy必 bring many difficulties. Therefore the sage treats everything as difficult, and so in the end has no difficulty.

original_text: 其安易持，其未兆易謀；其脆易泮，其微易散。為之於未有，治之於未亂。
translated_text: What is at rest is easy to hold. What has not yet arisen is easy to plan. What is brittle is easy to break. What is minute is easy to scatter. Act before things arise. Order before disorder sets in.

original_text: 合抱之木，生於毫末；九層之臺，起於累土；千里之行，始於足下。
translated_text: A tree that fills a man's embrace grows from a tiny sprout. A tower of nine stories rises from a heap of earth. A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath one's feet.

original_text: 為者敗之，執者失之。是以聖人無為故無敗，無執故無失。
translated_text: He who acts will fail. He who grasps will lose. Therefore the sage acts without failing and grasps without losing.

original_text: 民之從事，常於幾成而敗之。慎終如始，則無敗事。
translated_text: People in their affairs often fail just before completion. If one is as careful at the end as at the beginning, there will be no failure.

original_text: 是以聖人欲不欲，不貴難得之貨；學不學，復眾人之所過，以輔萬物之自然而不敢為。
translated_text: Therefore the sage desires what others do not desire and does not value rare goods. He learns what others do not learn and returns to what people have passed over. He supports the naturalness of all things and dares not act.

original_text: 古之善為道者，非以明民，將以愚之。
translated_text: In ancient times those who practiced the Tao did not use it to enlighten the people, but to keep them simple.

original_text: 民之難治，以其智多。故以智治國，國之賊；不以智治國，國之福。
translated_text: The reason people are hard to govern is that they have too much cleverness. Therefore he who governs with cleverness harms the state. He who does not govern with cleverness blesses the state.

original_text: 知此兩者亦稽式。常知稽式，是謂玄德。
translated_text: To know these two is also to know the model. To always know the model is called profound virtue.

original_text: 玄德深矣，遠矣，與物反矣，然後乃至大順。
translated_text: Profound virtue is deep and far-reaching. It turns all things back to their root and then reaches great harmony.

original_text: 江海之所以能為百谷王者，以其善下之，故能為百谷王。
translated_text: The reason rivers and seas can be king of the valleys is that they are good at making themselves lower. Therefore they can be king of the valleys.

original_text: 是以欲上民，必以言下之；欲先民，必以身後之。
translated_text: Therefore to place yourself above the people, you must speak humbly to them. To lead the people, you must put yourself behind them.

original_text: 是以聖人處上而民不重，處前而民不害。是以天下樂推而不厭。
translated_text: Therefore the sage stays above and the people are not burdened. He stays ahead and the people are not harmed. Therefore all under heaven love to promote him without getting tired of it.

original_text: 以其不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。
translated_text: It is precisely because he does not compete that no one under heaven can compete with him.

original_text: 天下皆謂我道大，似不肖。夫唯大，故似不肖。若肖，久矣其細也夫！
translated_text: All under heaven say my Tao is great but does not resemble anything. It is precisely because it is great that it does not resemble anything. If it resembled anything, it would long ago have become small.

original_text: 我有三寶，持而保之。一曰慈，二曰儉，三曰不敢為天下先。
translated_text: I have three treasures that I hold and protect. The first is compassion. The second is frugality. The third is not daring to come first under heaven.

original_text: 慈故能勇；儉故能廣；不敢為天下先，故能成器長。
translated_text: Because of compassion, one can be brave. Because of frugality, one can be generous. Because one does not dare to come first under heaven, one can become the chief of all things.

original_text: 今舍慈且勇；舍儉且廣；舍後且先；死矣！夫慈，以戰則勝，以守則固。天將救之，以慈衛之。
translated_text: Now if you abandon compassion and pursue bravery, abandon frugality and pursue generosity, abandon the last and pursue the first, you will die! Compassion — in battle it brings victory. In defense it brings strength. Heaven will save you, protecting you with compassion.

original_text: 善為士者，不武；善戰者，不怒；善勝敵者，不與；善用人者，為之下。
translated_text: A good soldier is not violent. A good fighter is not angry. A good winner is not vengeful. A good employer is humble.

original_text: 是謂不爭之德，是謂用人之力，是謂配天古之極。
translated_text: This is called the virtue of not competing, the ability to use the strength of others, and the matching of heaven's ancient perfection.

original_text: 用兵有言：吾不敢為主，而為客；不敢進寸，而退尺。
translated_text: There is a saying about the use of troops: I dare not be the host, but prefer to be the guest. I dare not advance an inch, but prefer to retreat a foot.

original_text: 是謂行無行；攘無臂；扔無敵；執無兵。
translated_text: This is called marching without marching, rolling up sleeves without arms, grasping without an enemy, wielding no weapon.

original_text: 禍莫大於輕敵；輕敵幾喪吾寶。
translated_text: No disaster is greater than underestimating the enemy. Underestimating the enemy nearly cost me my treasures.

original_text: 故抗兵相若，哀者勝矣。
translated_text: Therefore when opposing forces are evenly matched, the compassionate side wins.

original_text: 吾言甚易知，甚易行。天下莫能知，莫能行。
translated_text: My words are very easy to understand and very easy to practice. Yet no one under heaven can understand them or practice them.

original_text: 言有宗，事有君。夫唯無知，是以不我知。
translated_text: Words have an ancestor. Affairs have a master. It is precisely because of ignorance that they do not know me.

original_text: 知我者希，則我者貴。是以聖人被褐而懷玉。
translated_text: Those who know me are rare. Those who follow me are precious. Therefore the sage wears rough cloth and carries jade within.

original_text: 知不知，尚矣；不知知，病也。
translated_text: To know that you do not know is best. To not know and yet think you know is a disease.

original_text: 聖人不病，以其病病。夫唯病病，是以不病。
translated_text: The sage is free from this disease because he recognizes it as a disease. Precisely because he recognizes it as a disease, he is free from it.

original_text: 民不畏威，則大威至。
translated_text: When the people no longer fear authority, then a greater authority will come.

original_text: 無狎其所居，無厭其所生。夫唯不厭，是以不厭。
translated_text: Do not encroach upon their homes. Do not oppress their livelihoods. It is precisely because you do not oppress them that they will not be oppressed.

original_text: 是以聖人自知不自見；自愛不自貴。故去彼取此。
translated_text: Therefore the sage knows himself but does not show himself. He loves himself but does not exalt himself. He lets go of that and chooses this.

original_text: 勇於敢則殺，勇於不敢則活。此兩者，或利或害。天之所惡，孰知其故？
translated_text: Courage in daring leads to killing. Courage in not daring leads to life. Of these two, one is beneficial and one is harmful. What heaven detests — who knows the reason?

original_text: 天之道，不爭而善勝，不言而自應，不召而自來，繟然而善謀。
translated_text: The Tao of heaven does not compete and yet skillfully wins. It does not speak and yet responds on its own. It does not summon and yet comes of its own accord. It is relaxed and yet skillfully plans.

original_text: 天網恢恢，疏而不失。
translated_text: The net of heaven is vast. Though its mesh is wide, nothing slips through.

original_text: 民不畏死，奈何以死懼之？
translated_text: When the people no longer fear death, what is the use of threatening them with death?

original_text: 若使民常畏死，而為奇者，吾得執而殺之，孰敢？
translated_text: If the people could always be made to fear death, and there were those who acted in defiance, I could seize and execute them. Who would then dare?

original_text: 常有司殺者殺。夫代司殺者殺，是謂代大匠斫，夫代大匠斫者，希有不傷其手矣。
translated_text: There is always the master executioner who kills. To take the place of the master executioner and try to kill is like taking the place of the master carpenter and trying to cut. Those who take the place of the master carpenter rarely do not cut their own hands.

original_text: 民之飢，以其上食稅之多，是以飢。
translated_text: The people starve because those above them are greedy for taxes. Therefore they starve.

original_text: 民之難治，以其上之有為，是以難治。
translated_text: The people are hard to govern because those above them meddle. Therefore they are hard to govern.

original_text: 民之輕死，以其上求生之厚，是以輕死。
translated_text: The people make light of death because those above them try too hard to sustain life. Therefore they make light of death.

original_text: 人之生也柔弱，其死也堅強。草木之生也柔脆，其死也枯槁。
translated_text: A man at birth is soft and weak; at death he is hard and strong. Plants at birth are soft and tender; at death they are withered and dry.

original_text: 故堅強者死之徒，柔弱者生之徒。
translated_text: Therefore the hard and strong are followers of death. The soft and weak are followers of life.

original_text: 是以兵強則滅，木強則折。
translated_text: Therefore an army that is too strong will be destroyed. A tree that is too strong will be broken.

original_text: 強大處下，柔弱處上。
translated_text: The great and strong take the lower place. The soft and weak take the higher place.

original_text: 天之道，其猶張弓歟？高者抑之，下者舉之；有餘者損之，不足者補之。
translated_text: The Tao of heaven — is it not like the bending of a bow? The high is lowered, the low is raised. The excess is reduced, the deficient is supplemented.

original_text: 天之道，損有餘而補不足。人之道則不然，損不足以奉有餘。
translated_text: The Tao of heaven reduces what is excessive and supplements what is deficient. The way of man is not so. It reduces what is deficient to offer to what is excessive.

original_text: 孰能有餘以奉天下，唯有道者。
translated_text: Who can take what is excessive and offer it to the world? Only one who has the Tao.

original_text: 是以聖人為而不恃，功成而不處，其不欲見賢。
translated_text: Therefore the sage acts but does not possess, accomplishes but does not claim credit. He does not wish to display his excellence.

original_text: 天下莫柔弱於水，而攻堅強者莫之能勝，以其無以易之。
translated_text: Nothing under heaven is softer and weaker than water, yet nothing is better at overcoming the hard and strong. This is because nothing can replace it.

original_text: 弱之勝強，柔之勝剛，天下莫不知，莫能行。
translated_text: The weak overcomes the strong. The soft overcomes the hard. Everyone under heaven knows this, yet no one can practice it.

original_text: 是以聖人云：受國之垢，是謂社稷主；受國不祥，是為天下王。正言若反。
translated_text: Therefore the sage says: To bear the filth of the state is called the lord of the altars. To bear the misfortune of the state is called the king of the world. True words seem to be inverted.

original_text: 和大怨，必有餘怨；安可以為善？
translated_text: To reconcile a great resentment must leave residual resentment. How can this be called good?

original_text: 是以聖人執左契，而不責於人。有德司契，無德司徹。
translated_text: Therefore the sage holds the left tally but does not demand payment from others. The virtuous attend to the tally. The unvirtuous attend to the collection.

original_text: 天道無親，常與善人。
translated_text: The Tao of heaven has no favorites. It is always with the good person.

original_text: 小國寡民。使有什伯之器而不用；使民重死而不遠徙。
translated_text: Let the state be small and the people few. Though they have tools of ten and a hundred, they will not use them. Let the people take death seriously and not migrate far.

original_text: 雖有舟輿，無所乘之；雖有甲兵，無所陳之。使民復結繩而用之。
translated_text: Though they have boats and carriages, no one rides in them. Though they have armor and weapons, no one displays them. Let the people return to using knotted cords.

original_text: 甘其食，美其服，安其居，樂其俗。
translated_text: They find their food sweet, their clothes beautiful, their homes comfortable, their customs enjoyable.

original_text: 鄰國相望，雞犬之聲相聞，民至老死，不相往來。
translated_text: Neighboring states are within sight. The sounds of chickens and dogs are heard. The people grow old and die without having visited one another.

original_text: 信言不美，美言不信。
translated_text: Truthful words are not beautiful. Beautiful words are not truthful.

original_text: 善者不辯，辯者不善。知者不博，博者不知。
translated_text: The good are not eloquent. The eloquent are not good. The wise are not learned. The learned are not wise.

original_text: 聖人不積，既以為人己愈有，既以與人己愈多。天之道，利而不害；聖人之道，為而不爭。
translated_text: The sage does not accumulate. The more he does for others, the more he has. The more he gives to others, the more he gains. The Tao of heaven benefits all things and does not harm them. The way of the sage is to act without competing.
